sentences.text: The Payload Processing Facility is responsible for transforming downlinked payload telemetry into image products that are traceable to the source telemetry and to the processing configuration used at execution time.

Raw transfer starts when station delivery files arrive with an accompanying manifest, and the ingest workflow verifies file size, sequence continuity, checksum, and acquisition time before processing is scheduled.
The Telemetry Ingest Service writes accepted raw data to immutable staging storage and records the session identifier used by downstream processors.
Corrupted or incomplete raw segments are isolated from the nominal queue, and the operator display shows whether recovery, retransmission, or discard is required.
The Primary Processing Cluster generates Level 0 products by removing transfer framing, ordering source packets, and preserving instrument time tags without radiometric or geometric correction.
Level 1A processing reconstructs detector samples and appends engineering context, while Level 1B processing applies radiometric calibration and sensor model parameters.
Level 2 processing applies geolocation, atmospheric screening where applicable, and gridding rules defined in the active product specification.
Each processing level records software build identifiers, calibration baseline identifiers, and ancillary input versions so that a product can be regenerated under audit.
The Long Term Archive is also known as Granite in operator procedures for storage capacity and retrieval coordination.
Released products are stored in the Long Term Archive with metadata that distinguish operational output from test output and reprocessed output.
The Payload Calibration Team maintains the approved calibration baseline and reviews trend evidence before a new baseline is made eligible for operational use.
The Product Quality Service uses the patch bundle to update calibration applicability checks before the next product assessment cycle.
Calibration changes are first applied to a controlled sample of recent scenes, and the resulting metrics are compared with the current operational baseline.
If a calibration change alters radiometric scale, geometric alignment, or saturation behavior, affected product specifications are updated before general release resumes.
The Product Quality Service assigns quality flags for missing source packets, timing discontinuity, saturation, cloud screening uncertainty, geolocation residuals, and processing fallback.
Quality flags are encoded in product metadata and summary records so that automated consumers can reject, warn, or accept data consistently.
A product is placed in a delivery hold state when mandatory checks fail, required ancillary data are missing, or an operator opens a blocking review.
The Product Quality Service produces the Product Hold List when release blocking defects must be tracked across scenes and processing levels.
Held products remain reproducible in staging storage, but they are not promoted for user delivery until the blocking condition has been cleared.
The Network Control System uses the Security Exception Ticket to restrict affected transfer paths until approved containment actions are complete.
Lantern shall preserve the last validated routing configuration and reject unreviewed changes while payload product transfers are active.
When the Primary Processing Cluster cannot meet the processing window, the scheduling service assigns eligible jobs to the Backup Processing Cluster using the same container image and rule set.
The Backup Processing Cluster writes provenance that identifies the fallback execution path, and the Product Quality Service treats that marker as an input to its quality decision.
The Long Term Archive sends the Storage Watermark Snapshot after each daily storage assessment.
If both clusters are unavailable, processing is suspended, raw data are preserved in staging, and Mission Control Center is notified through the normal operational event channel.
Recovery after suspension prioritizes products with contractual latency commitments, then processes remaining scenes in acquisition order unless mission management approves a different backlog rule.
